other_peer_applied.scope: diffuse Walsh stress test and fiber-supremum dimension loss

mathematical_change.statement: For independent coordinate densities <=1, an orthonormal n-by-k frame U with k>=3 and every row leverage <=1/2, large coefficients |lambda_j|>=1, and arbitrary measurable coordinate-separable perturbations sum_i V_i(X_i), the variable sum_i V_i(X_i)+(U^T X)^T Lambda(U^T X) has a bounded continuous density with norm <= e*k/(k-2) <=3e.
mathematical_change.mechanism: unimodular coordinate phases preserve all one-coordinate Lp norms, so sharp Hausdorff-Young plus geometric Brascamp-Lieb gives a uniform L1 bound for the projected complex measure; Fresnel inversion yields integrable t^{-k/2} decay.
mathematical_change.quadratic_corollary: A=D+U Lambda U^T with arbitrary diagonal D obeys the same bound under the diffuse-frame hypotheses.

stress_test: For the rank-three Walsh frame, c_i=3/n; hence n>=6 is covered with C=3e despite tiny fixed-size coordinate compressions.

unresolved_implication.statement: For A=U Lambda U^T+C with CU=0 and diffuse U, control the nonseparable residual phase x^T C x without losing product normalization; separately bridge leverage-heavy rows.
